transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello, Mr. Okonkwo. I wanted to come in and talk to you about how you're feeling and what happened with the reaction you had to the medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am feeling better now, thank you. But I am still wondering why my skin turned that way. It was very frightening.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I've looked into it. There was a medication error. I prescribed the drug without checking your allergy list, and the pharmacy dispensed it. We gave you something you are allergic to.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Allergic? But I have told this hospital many times. I have a card in my wallet for this reason.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. I'm sorry for any confusion this caused. We were really busy on the ward last night and it seems the check was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? This was not confusion. This was a mistake. I am a man of standing in my community. If people knew I was here because of a mistake, it would be embarrassing. My family... they see me as the one who handles everything.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell that you're feeling very distressed and worried about how this reflects on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just about the rash. It is the thought that I am not safe here. Who is watching me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was an oversight in the electronic health record interaction. The contraindication wasn't flagged in the immediate view during the order entry.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not know what a contraindication is. Please speak plainly.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It means the drug and the allergy don't mix. It should have stopped the order.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you didn't see the allergy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very shaken. I cannot imagine what would have happened if I had been alone in the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that it is scary. But listen, I actually have to go check on another patient right now, so let's just try to move forward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are leaving? Now? I have not finished telling you how I feel.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just mean we can continue this later.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is how you treat a man who almost had a severe reaction because of your mistake? You are rushing away?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry, I just have a very tight schedule today. I just wanted to make sure you knew what happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And what happens now? How do I know this won't happen again tomorrow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. What specifically is being done?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, we'll see how the rest of the day goes and I'll probably check your chart again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want to know who is responsible for ensuring my safety for the rest of my stay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just stay tuned for now. I'm sure the team will be more careful.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very disappointing. I thought we had a good relationship.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We do, but I really have to get to that other room. We can talk more later.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('I actually have to go', 'tight schedule', 'have to get to that other room') and dismisses the patient's emotional bids.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly and early, but the resident used medical jargon ('contraindication') and never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: The resident apologizes, but immediately dilutes it with an excuse regarding being 'really busy on the ward last night'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('distressed and worried') and acknowledges the patient's fear, though later dismisses the patient's needs.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague assurances ('keep an eye on it', 'stay tuned', 'probably check your chart') with no concrete plan.
